chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How is the greeting to be upon the inhabitants of the graves?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say.'
Peace be upon the inhabitants of the houses, from the Muslims and the Believers. May Allah have mercy on the preceding ones from us and the delayed ones, and we, if Allah wills, are joining with you.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ: The delayed ones (those who will die later)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ: The preceding ones (those who died earlier)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct Islamic supplication to recite when visiting graves?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the canonical formula for *Ziyarat al-Qubur*, emphasizing the continuity of the believer's journey through the invocation of peace upon both past and future generations of Muslims. Scholarly tradition highlights the phrase 'those who preceded us and those who will follow' as a theological affirmation of the communal nature of the afterlife and the inevitability of death, reinforcing the concept of *Barzakh* as a transitional state where the deceased remain accessible to the living's supplications. The formula serves not only as a ritual greeting but as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the eternal reality of the Hereafter.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How are the greetings to be upon the inhabitants of the graves?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be saying:

‘The greetings be upon you, O inhabitants of the houses, from the Muslims and the Believers. May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on the preceding ones from us, and the delayed ones, and we, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing, would be joining with you’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mada’iniy who has said the following:
“I asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’How should one offer greeting of peace to the people of the graves?’ He replied, say,

‘May Allah grant peace to the Muslims and believing ones of this dwelling place. May Allah grant mercy upon those of us who have preceded us (to the next life) and those who will follow and we, by the will of Allah, are about to join you.’”
